page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.gn5i-c8g1.2xlarge is a GPU-accelerated virtual machine instance powered by the KVM hypervisor. It features 8 dedicated vCPUs mapped to 8 physical cores using an Intel Xeon E5-2682 v4 processor running at 2.5 GHz. The system is equipped with 32.0 GB of system memory, providing a balanced 4.0 GB of RAM per core. Acceleration is delivered via a single integrated NVIDIA Pascal P4 GPU with 8 GB of dedicated VRAM.

This instance type does not include local NVMe or SSD storage, requiring external block storage volumes for persistent data. Network connectivity is limited to a baseline bandwidth of 2 Gbps. The x86_64 CPU architecture supports AVX, AES, BMI2, and FMA instruction sets, but lacks newer AVX-512 extensions such as AVX512F or AVX512_VNNI, which limits its efficiency in modern vectorized workloads.

Performance benchmarks indicate that the underlying hardware belongs to an older generation. The stress-ng single-core CPU performance falls into the bottom 10 percent, while multi-core CPU performance and memory bandwidth tests consistently rank in the bottom 25 percent. PassMark CPU scores sit in the middle 50 percent range, but database operations, Redis SET throughput, and static web serving benchmarks remain in the bottom quartile. These results highlight a significant performance tradeoff, where CPU-bound and memory-bound tasks exhibit lower throughput compared to newer architecture classes.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the ecs.gn5i-c8g1.2xlarge offers entry-level GPU acceleration without the premium cost of modern high-end accelerators. It is suitable for legacy GPU-accelerated workloads, basic machine learning inference, video transcoding, and lightweight parallel processing tasks that require CUDA support but do not demand high-speed memory bandwidth or local storage performance.
